To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GM-CSF is a potent chemokine for the recruitment of DC and that GM-CSF in a bioadhesive gel is able to stimulate the migration of DC in organotypically cultured HPV-transformed keratinoctyes and in a human (p) neoplastic epithelum grafted onto NOD/SCIDS mice.
the bioadhesive polyelectrolyte gel is an efficient carrier for GM-CSF and is a potent factor in stimulating the infiltration of DC/LC into HPV-induced epithelial lesions.

GM-CSF in bioadhesive polyelectrolyte gel is a potent agent in enhancing DC/LC recruitment in HPV-associated (preneoplastic lesions and that the efficacy of this formulation is equivalent to that observed in liquid GM-CSF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel immunotherapeutic approaches for genital HPV-associated lesions.

the development of novel pharmaceutical formulations to deliver cytokines in the genital tract, which could be of interest to stimulate the immune response against HPV-associated (preneoplastic) lesions.
the development of a novel topical formulation of GM-CSF that can enhance the recruitment of DC in (pre)neoplasic lesions of the uterine cervix.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GM-CSF is a potent stimulator of the migration of DC into HPV-transformed human keratinocytes and that this effect could be obtained by using a polycarbophil bioadhesive hydrogel.

GM-CSF is a potent stimulant of DC migration into the epithelium, and that the delivery of GM-CSF incorporated into a bioadhesive gel is effective for the recruitment of DC in models of HPV-associated (pre)cancerous lesions.
the use of a bioadhesive hydrogel containing GM-CSF could be useful in the treatment of genital HPV lesions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GM-CSF delivered by a bioadhesive hydrogel stimulates the migration of dendritic cells in organotypic models of (pre)neoplastical epithelial lesions.
GM-CSF in polycarbopol gel could be a useful tool for the recruitment of DC in mucosal surfaces.

the bioadhesive hydrogel delivery of GM-CSF is a potent factor in the recruitment of dendritic cells into (pre)neoplasic epithelial lesions, and thus, could be used in a new immunotheraputic approach against genital HPV-associated (Pre)neoplastic diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

GM-CSF can be delivered to the skin in a bioactive form by a bioadhesive hydrogel and that the delivery of GM-CSF can stimulate the migration of dendritic cells into HPV-associated (pre)- neoplastic epithelial lesions.
the delivery of GM-CSF using a bioadhesive hydrogel is a very efficient way to recruit dendritic cells into HPV-transformed kerati-nocytes.
GM-CSF can be delivered to the skin using a polymer gel and that the gel can enhance the recruitment of Langerhans Cells to the skin, which may be useful in the treatment of skin cancer.
